solution: In this sentence, the verb should be in the passive voice, which requires the past participle form of the verb. “Is allows” is incorrect because “allows” is the present tense, which doesn’t match the required passive construction. The phrase “is allowed” correctly follows the subject-verb agree- ment, making it the grammatically correct choice.

subject: English
stem: The dessert was \(\underline{\text{many sweet}}\) for my tastes.
solution: The correct phrase is “too sweet,” which indicates that the dessert was excessively sweet for the speaker. “Many sweet” is incorrect because “many” is used with countable nouns, while “sweet” is an uncountable adjective in this context. The other options, “to sweetly” and “more sweeter,” are grammatically incorrect.

subject: English
stem: The sea wall protected the \(\underline{\text{village in}}\) the waves.
solution: The sentence expresses the idea that the seawall protected the village from the waves, which is the proper preposition to indicate protection against something. “In the waves” does not convey the intended meaning, as it suggests the village is in the waves, which isn’t correct. The other options, “village through” and “village by,” do not fit grammatically in this context either.

subject: English
stem: Since 1950 the number of children in secondary schools \(\underline{\text{has been increasing noticeable}}\).
solution: The sentence is in the present perfect continuous tense (“has been increasing”), which indicates an ongoing action that started in the past and continues into the present. The adverb “noticeably” should be placed correctly after the verb “increasing” to describe the extent of the increase. “Noticeable” is an adjective, which is incorrect here because we need an adverb to modify the verb.

subject: English

solution: The term “Verbose” refers to someone who uses more words than necessary, often speaking at length. This matches the meaning of “talkative,” which describes a person who talks a lot. The other options are not synonyms: “aggressive” refers to being forceful or hostile, “decisive” refers to being clear and firm in decision-making, and “exhaustive” means thorough, which is unrelated to the idea of talking.

subject: English
stem: His \(\underline{\text{MODEST}}\) nature made all the difference.
solution: “Modest” refers to someone humble or not boastful. “Shy” can be a similar trait, as both can describe someone who does not seek attention or prefers not to stand out. The other options are not synonyms: “courageous” means brave, “horrific” means causing fear or dread, and “dry” refers to something lacking moisture or being dull.

The other options are not synonyms: “alleviate” means to reduce or ease something (typically pain), “energise” means to give energy or vitality, and “elevate” means to raise or lift something, neither of which fits the context of feeling weakened.

solution: The quorum requirement in the Rajya Sabha is 25 members, which is one-tenth of the total members of the House (Article 100). This is established by the Constitution for both the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.

solution: President of India has the power to declare war or peace. The prime minister and his ministers must recommend him to declare war or make peace (Article 352).

subject: Polity
chapter: Government Structure — Parliament, Judiciary and Constitutional Bodies
stem: The Vice-President of India can be removed from the office:
optA: by a resolution initiated by the Council of States and approved by the Lok Sabha.
optB: by a resolution in the Lok Sabha agreed to by the Council of States.
optC: by a resolution adopted by the two Houses meetings in a joint session.
optD: following a formal process of impeachment.
solution: The Vice-President can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an absolute majority and agreed to by a simple majority of the Lok Sabha. But no such resolution may be moved unless at least 14 days advance notice has been given.

subject: Polity
chapter: Government Structure — Parliament, Judiciary and Constitutional Bodies
stem: In India, the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of:
optA: members of both Houses of Parliament.
optB: elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
optC: elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the State Legislative Assemblies.
optD: members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies.
solution: The Vice President is indirectly chosen by members of an electoral college composed of representatives of both Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of Proportional Representation by means of a single transferable vote and voted by secret ballot by the election commission. The Vice President of India also serves as the Honorable Chancellor of the University of Punjab, Chandigarh. The Vice President of India, after the President, is India’s second-highest constitutional office. Article 63 of the Indian Constitution specifies that ‘There shall be a Vice President of India.’

stem: On a particular day, 120 members of the Rajya Sabha were present for a meeting of the Rajya Sabha to vote on an ordinary bill already passed by the Lok Sabha. Seventy five members vote for the bill. In this context which one of the following possibilities is correct?
optA: The bill fails to pass because half the number of members of Rajya Sabha were not present and did not vote.

optD: The bill is not passed and has to go to the Lower House for reconsideration.
solution: The minimum number of members required to pass a bill in the Rajya Sabha depends on the type of bill: Ordinary bill: A simple majority of members present and voting is required Constitution amendment bill: A majority of the total membership of the house and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting is required in each house of Parliament After passing through both houses, the President’s assent is required.

stem: According to the Constitution of India, a new All India Service can be instituted, with the initiative taken by:
optA: more than two-thirds of the States
solution: Under Article 312 of the Indian Constitution, the Rajya Sabha holds the authority to initiate the establishment of new All–India Services. This is achieved through a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting. Importantly, the process does not require direct approval from individual states but is undertaken by the Union Parliament. Once the resolution is approved by the Rajya Sabha, it is forwarded to the Lok Sabha for further legislative action.

solution: To qualify as a candidate for the office of the President of India, the nomination papers must have the signatures of at least 50 proposers and 50 seconders from the Electoral College. The Electoral College comprises the elected members of both Houses of Parliament, as well as the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories with legislatures. This rule ensures that only candidates with significant support are considered for the election.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Exfoliation of rock takes place due to:
solution: Exfoliation of rocks, also known as on- ion-skin weathering, occurs due to thermal expan- sion and contraction. This process is most common in regions with significant temperature fluctuations, such as deserts. During the day, rocks expand due to heat, and at night, they contract due to cooling. Over time, this repeated expansion and contraction causes the outer layers of the rock to peel off, much like the layers of an onion.

subject: Geography

stem: The type of igneous rocks which are formed midway between volcanic and plutonic rocks, are known as:
solution: Hypabyssal rocks are igneous rocks that are formed between volcanic and plutonic rocks. They are intrusive igneous rocks that solidify at medium to shallow depths within the Earth’s crust. Hypabyssal rocks have an intermediate grain size and texture between intrusive and extrusive rocks.

solution: The lightest layer of the Earth is the Sial layer: The uppermost layer of the Earth’s crust, made of silicate and aluminium. It’s also known as the “continental crust”. Sial is the lightest layer of the Earth, with a specific gravity of 2.7 to 2.9 g/cm3.

subject: Geography

stem: The pieces of rocks that are shattered by frost action, embedded in the glaciers and brought down by them are called:
solution: Moraines: Frost weathering is the process of rocks breaking due to freezing. Frost cracking, also known as frost riving or frost splitting, occurs when water soaks into the crevices of hard rocks during the thaw season. When the temperature drops, the water freezes and causes the rocks to split. When a glacier melts, the rock fragments that were dragged along beneath the frozen ice are dropped and spread across the valley floor as ground moraine. There are eight different types of moraine, which are categorized based on the type of material they are made up of and whether they are present after the glacier has melted or receded.

solution: Corrosion is the slow oxidation of metals by either oxygen or water. In the case of iron it is given by the equation: 4Fe + 3O2 + 2H2O — 2Fe2O3.2H2O The substance so formed is called hydrated ferric oxide. It forms an immediate layer on the surface of iron which degrades the properties of iron immediately. Hence, iron corrodes rapidly.

solution: The concentration of solution = Mass of common salt/Mass of solution × 100 Given • Mass of solute = 20 g • Mass of solvent= 180 g Mass of solution = 180 + 20 g = 200 g We know that, mass by mass percentage: Mass of solute/mass of solution × 100 Hence 10% 20/200 g × 100 → 10% • Thus, the correct answer is 10%.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The valency of an element depends upon the:

solution: Valency is a measure of an atom’s ability to combine with other atoms to form chemical compounds. The number of electrons in the valence shell determines how many electrons an atom will gain, lose, or share to become stable. Most atoms are stable when they have eight electrons in their outermost shell, which is known as completing their octet. Hydrogen and helium are exceptions, as they become stable when they complete their duplet.

However, the mission failed to resolve the constitutional deadlock, leading to the launch of the Quit India Movement. solution: Civil Disobedience Movement was launched by Gandhi in March 1930 (with the Dandi March) after Lord Irwin failed to act on the 11 point ultimatum. Salt was selected as the central formula as it attracted the support of almost all the sections of Indian population. After the publishing of Nehru Report in 1928, the Muslim League had distanced themselves from the Congress. Hence, the participation of Muslims was very low. Gandhi was influenced by David Thoreau’s essays on Civil Disobedience. The Dandi March was led by Gandhi where he violated the British salt laws. Similarly, in Tamilnadu, C Rajagopalachari led a march from Tiruchinapalli to Vedaranyam coast and violated the salt laws. Civil disobedience involved breaking of British laws, non-payment of revenue in the ryotwari areas, non-payment of chaukidari taxes (levied for the remuneration of village watchmen) in the zamindari areas and violation of forest laws in the Central provinces (going into reserve forests to collect wood and graze cattle). Gandhi ultimately withdrew the CDM in 1934 due to lack of support from the people.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Chandragupta I was the founder of the Gupta dynasty, establishing the Gupta Empire in India around 320 CE. His reign laid the groundwork for one of the most prosperous and culturally significant empires in Indian history. The Allahabad Pillar inscription (also called the Allahabad Pillar Edict of Samudragupta) records the military achievements of Samudragupta, not Chandragupta I. This inscription does not mention Chandragupta I’s conquests. While Chandragupta I’s influence extended primarily over northern and central India, the conquests detailed in the inscription are attributed to his successor, Samudragupta.

solution: The Nehru Report (1928) was the first significant Indian attempt to draft a constitutional framework for India. solution: Adrenaline is the hormone that increases the heartbeat in mammals.
